record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Can one perform a genuine string-theoretic computation of the one-point function of a non-protected operator in the defect AdS/CFT setup?

evidence.quote: Finally, an open problem is to perform a string theoretical computation of the one-point function of a non-protected operator.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the defect AdS/CFT setup obtained from the D3–D5 brane intersection: planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang–Mills theory in four dimensions with a codimension-one defect across which the gauge group rank jumps by $k$ units, dual on the string-theory side to type IIB string theory on $AdS_5\times S^5$ in the presence of a probe D5 brane wrapping an $AdS_4\times S^2$ submanifold and carrying $k$ units of background world-volume gauge-field flux through the $S^2$.

In this background, single-trace local gauge-invariant operators $\mathcal{O}(x)$ of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM acquire non-vanishing one-point functions
$$\langle \mathcal{O}(x)\rangle = \frac{C_{\mathcal{O}}}{|x_\perp|^{\Delta_{\mathcal{O}}}},$$
where $x_\perp$ is the distance to the defect and $\Delta_{\mathcal{O}}$ is the conformal dimension of $\mathcal{O}$. On the gauge-theory side, the coefficients $C_{\mathcal{O}}$ have been computed at tree level (and in some cases beyond) for both protected operators and a wide class of non-protected operators (e.g. non-BPS scalar operators in the $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ subsectors), where they admit closed-form expressions as overlaps between Bethe eigenstates of an integrable spin chain and a matrix product (boundary) state encoding the D5-brane.

On the string-theory side, the one-point functions of protected (chiral primary) operators can be reproduced by a semiclassical computation of the disk amplitude of a closed-string vertex operator ending on the probe D5 brane.

Problem. Perform a genuine first-principles string-theoretic computation of the one-point function $C_{\mathcal{O}}$ for a non-protected single-trace operator $\mathcal{O}$ in this defect AdS/CFT setup. Concretely, define and evaluate a worldsheet (disk) amplitude on $AdS_5\times S^5$ with boundary on the flux-carrying probe D5 brane, inserting a closed-string vertex operator that is dual to a non-BPS gauge-theory operator (for example, a non-BPS scalar operator in the $SU(2)$ subsector), and reproduce, or predict, the corresponding gauge-theory result for $C_{\mathcal{O}}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches return work on one-point functions of non-protected operators in D3–D5 defect CFT computed on the gauge-theory side via integrability and matrix-product-state overlaps, and a worldsheet integrable-boundary-state bootstrap program for non-BPS operators. However, no genuine first-principles string (worldsheet/disk) computation of a one-point function of a non-protected operator in the defect AdS/CFT setup appears to have been carried out; the problem is still regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: One-point Functions in Defect CFT and Integrability
status_evidence.snippet: One-point functions of non-protected operators in the defect CFT dual to the D3-D5 brane system with k units of world volume flux calculated at tree level via spin-chain/MPS overlaps.
status_evidence.claim: Gauge-theory-side computations for non-protected operators are well developed via integrability, but the string-theory disk computation is not given there.

status_evidence.title: Integrable boundary states in D3-D5 dCFT: beyond scalars
status_evidence.snippet: A non-perturbative bootstrap-type program for integrable boundary states on the worldsheet of the IIB string theory has been developed for general non-BPS operators.
status_evidence.claim: Worldsheet treatments use integrable boundary-state bootstrap rather than a direct disk-amplitude computation, indicating the genuine string-theoretic computation remains open.
